about: What craftcheck.py measures and when it reports it: the code-craft rules of craft.md that a scan can see. Limits are inclusive (a function of 31 lines is over a limit of 30). Each rule names its id in craft.md, its severity, the words a non-developer reads and the fix.

long_function.title: Long functions
long_function.why: a function that does many things is hard to read, test and change without breaking something else
long_function.fix: split it into small functions that each do one thing, named for what they do (extract method)

many_params.title: Functions with many arguments
many_params.why: every argument is one more thing to understand and to get in the right order
many_params.fix: pass one object that groups the values that belong together, or split the function

flag_param.title: A true/false argument that switches behaviour
flag_param.why: a flag says the function does two things; callers read foo(true) and cannot tell what it means
flag_param.fix: make two functions with names that say what each one does

deep_nesting.title: Deeply nested code
deep_nesting.why: if inside if inside loop: the reader has to keep every level in mind at once
deep_nesting.fix: return early for the simple cases (guard clauses) and move inner blocks into functions of their own

type_switch.title: A long switch or if/else chain
type_switch.why: every new case means opening this code again; the same chain tends to appear in more places
type_switch.fix: when it chooses by kind or state: polymorphism, a Strategy or State object, or a lookup table (Open/Closed)

large_class.title: Classes with many methods
large_class.why: a class with many jobs changes for many reasons (Single Responsibility) and every change risks the others
large_class.fix: split it by responsibility; let each class keep the data it works on (Information Expert, High Cohesion)

swallowed_error.title: Errors caught and ignored
swallowed_error.why: an empty catch hides failures: the app goes on with wrong data and nobody knows why
swallowed_error.fix: handle the error, log it with context, or let it reach a place that can tell the user

duplicate.title: Duplicated code
duplicate.why: the same lines in two places drift apart; a fix in one is forgotten in the other (Don't Repeat Yourself)
duplicate.fix: move the shared lines into one function or class and call it from both places

commented_code.title: Commented-out code
commented_code.why: dead code in comments rots: nobody dares to delete it and nobody knows if it still matters
commented_code.fix: delete it; git remembers the old version

train_wreck.title: Long chains of calls through other objects
train_wreck.why: a.getB().getC().getD() reaches through objects it should not know about (Law of Demeter), so a change deep inside breaks it
train_wreck.fix: ask the nearest object for what you need (tell, don't ask), or give it a method that does the work
